verses.1: In those days, Hezekiah fell ill and died. Then Yeshua ben Amoz, the prophet, came to him and said to him, “As the Lord has commanded your house, so it will be: you will die and will not live again.”
verses.2: And he turned his face toward the wall and prayed to Jehovah, saying:
verses.3: May the LORD remember what I have done before you. I have acted with truth and in good faith. I have done what is right in your eyes. May He strengthen me with His power.
verses.4: And Esau did not go out into the courtyard. The word of Jehovah was to him: “Do not go out.”
verses.5: Once again, you said to Jehizkiah, “I will say what the LORD, the God of David your father, has commanded me to say. I have heard your prayers; I have seen your tears. I am here to help you on the third day. You shall bring the house of the LORD.”
verses.6: And I have reigned over you for fifteen years. From the time of King Ashur, I have protected you and this city. I have guarded this city for my own sake and for the sake of David, my servant.
verses.7: And Sheba said, “Take some honey.” They took it and applied it to their wounds. And they recovered.
verses.8: And Hizkiah said to Jeshaiah, “What will God do for me?” On the third day, I entered the house of God.
verses.9: And Esaias said, “Go, and tell the people of Yehovah that Yehovah will do what he has promised. He will make it happen, even if it takes twelve times ten years.”
verses.10: And Jehizkiah said, “Let them pay twelve talents as a penalty. But do not let another person be punished for the same offense.”
verses.11: And the prophet Yeshayahu called out to Jehovah. He set aside those “tents” that had been placed on the hills. These tents were twelve in number.
verses.12: On that day, Baradach sent out men from Baladan to go to Hizkia. They brought gifts and offerings to Hizkia, because they heard that Hizkia was sick.
verses.13: And Hizkiah heard about them. He ordered that every house be searched thoroughly. All the money, gold, and silver objects were taken away. Also, all the good wine and all that was found in their treasures was taken away as well. Nothing was left behind in Hizkiah’s house or in his entire kingdom.
verses.14: And the prophet Yeshayahu went before King Hizkia. He said to him, “What did these people say? From where do they come to you?” Hizkia replied, “They come from a distant land, from Babylon.”
verses.15: And he said, “What did they see in your house? He said, “Zikriya, everything that was seen in my house was something that they never saw among my possessions.”
verses.16: And Esaiah said to Hizkia, “Hear the word of the LORD.”
verses.17: Now, days are coming when all that is in your houses and what your ancestors have stored up until today will be taken away. No more will anything be left by the words of Jehovah.
verses.18: And from your offspring who will come out of you, they will take them and make them servants in the palace of King Babylon.
verses.19: And Hezekiah said to Josiah, “What a good thing it is that Jehovah has spoken such words. And Josiah said, “May peace and truth be in my days.”
verses.20: And also all the words of Jezikia, and all his deeds. He also built the Temple and the Altar. He brought the waters to the city. These things are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.21: And Hizkiah slept with his fathers. And Menashe, his son, reigned in his place.
